notes: License policy for the Shera Bot private prototype. The gate fails on any dependency
whose license is neither in `allowed` nor named in `reviewedExceptions`.
`allowed` holds permissive licenses plus MPL-2.0 — weak, file-level copyleft with an
explicit linking permission (lightningcss, a Rust CSS tool pulled in by Next tooling).
`reviewedExceptions` holds licenses that are NOT generally allowed but have been
reviewed for named dependencies, with the obligation analysis written down. The
`packages` globs are enforced: an exception covers only matching package names, so the
same license on an unexpected package fails the gate rather than inheriting a rationale
Compound expressions are supported: `A OR B` passes when either side passes; `A AND B`
requires both sides; `A WITH B` is decided by the base license. Parenthesized or mixed
expressions require every component to be acceptable — stricter than SPDX on purpose,
so anything subtle fails closed and goes to a human.
Any addition to `reviewedExceptions` must also be recorded in the slice's engineering
This policy governs THIRD-PARTY dependencies only. The Pi fork's own license
obligations are tracked separately and are still open (see docs/TRACEABILITY.md).

reviewedExceptions.packagesNote: The prebuilt native binaries behind sharp (Next.js image optimization): @img/sharp-<platform>-<arch> and @img/sharp-libvips-<platform>-<arch>. The glob is deliberate, because the platform-specific package names differ between the Windows development machine and the Linux CI runner.
reviewedExceptions.rationale: Unmodified prebuilt native binary, loaded at runtime and not statically linked into our code. The prototype is private and not distributed, so the LGPL distribution obligations (source offer, relinking) are not triggered yet. Re-check before any distribution or public exposure at the Stage 7 production-readiness gate.
alternatives: Drop the image-optimization dependency and serve images unoptimized: loses Next.js image optimization for no prototype benefit.
Fail the gate on LGPL until distribution terms exist: blocks S01 on a dependency the owner has not yet ruled on.
Vendor and build the library from source: real maintenance cost for a private prototype.
